title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 14, 2026: KOSPI Gives Back Rally, Samsung SDI and Alaska LNG Rise
content:
KOSPI closed at 6,008.81, down 0.44%, barely holding the 6,000 level after giving back an early rally of more than 2%, and KOSDAQ closed at 823.88, down 1.57%, as ASML's soft quarterly sales and renewed foreign selling offset a rebound from the previous day's plunge. Individual themes still moved on their own news: Seoul Express Bus Terminal redevelopment hopes, Taiwan's participation in Alaska LNG, and Samsung SDI with the wider battery sector.

1. Rebound fades on foreign selling — KOSPI barely defends 6,000

Korean markets rebounded strongly early on the view that the previous day's plunge had been overdone. KOSPI rose as high as about 6,190, up more than 2%, but renewed foreign selling in the afternoon erased the gains. Sentiment toward chip stocks weakened again after Dutch chip equipment maker ASML's third-quarter sales came in slightly below market expectations, and caution ahead of U.S. inflation data and higher oil prices also weighed. KOSPI closed at 6,008.81 (-0.44%) and KOSDAQ at 823.88 (-1.57%). Foreign investors sold about 1.18 trillion won on the main market while institutions were net buyers, helping defend the 6,000 level.

2. Seoul Express Bus Terminal redevelopment hopes continue — terminal asset stocks rise

Hopes for a mixed-use redevelopment of the Seoul Express Bus Terminal resurfaced and lifted Dongyang Express and Cheonil Express, with interest continuing in Daesung Industrial and Sampyo Cement. Seoul is in pre-negotiation with Shinsegae Central City on moving the terminal underground and building a large mixed-use complex above it, which keeps hopes alive for a revaluation of the assets on the prime Gangnam site.

3. Taiwan joins Alaska LNG — steel pipe and steel stocks in focus again

U.S. President Donald Trump said on the 13th (U.S. time) that Taiwan will invest up to $4.4 billion in the Alaska LNG project and buy 30% of the gas produced over the next 20 years, raising hopes that the project becomes real. Taiwan's government also confirmed the investment of up to $4.4 billion and a long-term import plan. Expectations of higher demand for steel pipe, steel and valves in building the large LNG pipeline and terminal put Daehan Steel, TCC Steel, Hwaseong Valve and Hansun Engineering in focus, and buying spread to existing Alaska LNG-linked names such as Daeyang Metal, KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe, Nexteel, Hi-Steel and Kumkang Steel. Daeyang Metal rose to near its daily limit early on and Daehan Steel gained more than 20%.

4. Samsung SDI earnings hopes and North American ESS growth — the battery leader rises

One of the most notable sectors was batteries led by Samsung SDI. Brokerages forecast third-quarter revenue of 4.1 trillion won and operating profit of 212.5 billion won, suggesting results could beat market expectations, and analysts said expanding North American ESS (energy storage) business would be a key growth driver. Samsung SDI plans to take over its stake in the U.S. joint venture with GM, securing a 27 GWh North American battery production site of its own and adding an ESS line there, with demand for ESS expected to grow with AI data centers and renewable energy. Dip buying and rotation spread across the battery sector.

5. Solid-state battery hopes — ISU Specialty Chemical and Lake Materials rise

Along with Samsung SDI's strength, hopes for commercializing solid-state batteries returned. Solid-state batteries use a solid electrolyte instead of a liquid one to raise safety and energy density, and Samsung SDI is developing them as a next-generation technology. ISU Specialty Chemical, tied to lithium sulfide, a key raw material for sulfide-based solid-state batteries, and Lake Materials, pursuing solid-state battery materials, were in focus.

6. AI data center power demand — buying spreads across the ESS value chain

ESS-related stocks also moved strongly on Samsung SDI's North American ESS growth hopes and expectations of rising AI data center power demand. AI data centers use large amounts of power and need large-scale storage to stabilize the grid, so battery makers have been expanding ESS investment as a growth market beyond EVs. HT Robotics, Hanjung NCS and Shinsung ST, which supply ESS battery parts, thermal management and systems, were in focus.

7. Solid-state and ESS strength — rotation into battery materials and parts

With solid-state and ESS strong together, buying spread across battery materials and parts. Sungwoo, Eco&Dream, WCP, Top Material and Daejoo Electronic Materials were in focus, particularly Eco&Dream (precursors), WCP (separators) and Daejoo Electronic Materials (silicon anode materials), which are tied to higher energy density in next-generation batteries. Today's move in batteries was therefore not just a single Samsung SDI rally but a sector rotation running from cells to solid-state to ESS to materials and parts.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI rebound and then fade on Oct 14?
It rose as much as 2% early on the view that the prior drop was overdone, but ASML's slightly weak third-quarter sales, caution ahead of U.S. inflation data, higher oil prices and renewed foreign selling erased the gains. KOSPI closed at 6,008.81 (-0.44%).

Why did Alaska LNG stocks rise?
President Trump said Taiwan will invest up to $4.4 billion and buy 30% of the gas produced over 20 years, which raised hopes the project becomes real and lifted expectations of demand for steel pipe, steel and valves.

Why was Samsung SDI strong?
Brokerage forecasts suggested third-quarter results could beat expectations, and plans to take over its stake in the GM joint venture and add an ESS line in North America raised growth hopes.
